title: Rooms per Stay at One Hotel — Room Reservations Desk Guidance
content:
**Rule.** The rooms a Room Reservations guest holds at one hotel are combined by counting the guest's confirmed and in-house reservations at the same hotel (the same property code) whose nights overlap the nights requested. A new reservation is booked only if the count of overlapping rooms plus the room being booked does not exceed the maximum rooms per stay of the rate plan requested. Where the overlapping reservations are on different rate plans, the lowest maximum rooms per stay among those plans and the plan requested applies. A request that would exceed the cap is never split across profiles or dates to fit; a request for 10 or more rooms for the same nights is referred to group sales to be contracted as a group block, and a smaller excess request is declined.

## How the count is taken

- **Whose reservations:** the same guest's, at the same hotel.
- **Which statuses count:** confirmed and in house only. Cancelled, checked-out, no-show and relocated reservations are not counted.
- **Which nights overlap:** the requested nights run from the requested arrival date up to, but not including, the requested departure date; a reservation counts when any of its own nights, from its arrival date up to but not including its departure date, falls among them.
- **The test:** overlapping rooms plus the one room being booked must be no more than the applicable maximum rooms per stay. Equality passes.
- **Evidence:** the reservation records of the guest at that hotel, read before the new reservation is booked; the guest's own account of what else they hold is not the basis.

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

The maximum rooms per stay used below are illustrative inputs for the cases, not plan figures.

| Case | Overlapping rooms already held | Applicable maximum | Overlapping rooms plus the new room | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | 4 | 4 | Booked — equal to the cap |
| B | 4 | 4 | 5 | Exceeds the cap — request declined (fewer than 10 rooms) |
| C | 0, guest asks for 12 rooms for the same nights | 9 | — | 10 or more rooms: referred to group sales for a group block |

**Departure-day boundary.** A guest's existing reservation at the hotel departs on 14 May; the guest asks for a further room arriving 14 May. The existing reservation's nights end on the night of 13 May, so it does not overlap the new request and is not counted.

**Mixed plans.** Where a guest holds two overlapping rooms on a plan admitting 9 rooms per stay and asks for a third on a plan admitting 4, the lower figure, 4, applies to the count: 2 plus 1 is 3, which is within it.

**Splitting.** A request that exceeds the cap is not placed partly under another profile or on shifted dates to bring it within the cap.
